item: run_open and run_refusals_net take their state inside the try that gives it back (R171)
summary: Q's scan of every @contextmanager for a take before its try (tests/test_contextmanager_acquire_before_try.py) named the two context managers the run records added. run_refusals_net set the refusal-scope variable before its try, so an interrupt in that gap left a scope nobody reset as the thread's current one and every later net nested under it; run_open wrote the run OPEN and read the free bytes before its try, so the same gap left a run 'open' (still going) for the life of the process. Both now make and set their state inside the try. The net's finally puts the PARENT scope back by asking the variable instead of undoing a token, so it needs no flag to say whether the set happened; its handlers record nothing when the scope was never made (an error before it exists is the caller's). run_open's note is None until run_started has returned and run_ended does nothing for None, so the finally ends the run it opened and a gap before the write leaves no run at all. Stated limit: an interrupt between the journal write inside run_started and the store of its return value still leaves the run open, which reads as 'started, never ended' (true of a process the interrupt ends). 7 tests deliver the interrupt just after the real step (a stand-in that does the set, or the free-space read, and then raises); the three that reach the gap fail on the old code (the others guard the branches the change added and the behaviour that did not change). The scan, not a test, is what tells run_started-before-the-try from run_started-inside-it: the two behave alike for the note a handler sees, so no test of behaviour can separate them.
